sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Geological Time Scale (GTS)**: A standardized system used by geologists and paleontologists to describe the timing and relationships of events that have occurred during Earth's history.
• **Stratigraphy & Biostratigraphy**: The study of rock layers (**strata**) and fossil succession (**Index Fossils**), which forms the empirical basis for dividing Earth's history into distinct geological intervals.
• **Deep Time Principle**: James Hutton's concept establishing that geological forces operating over immense spans of time have shaped the Earth, replacing catastrophism with **uniformitarianism** ('the present is the key to the past').
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Earth's history is divided into four major Eons: Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic (together comprising the **Precambrian Supereon**, representing ~88% of Earth's history), and Phanerozoic.

items.definition: An evolutionary event approximately 541 million years ago during which most major animal phyla appeared abruptly in the fossil record, marking the start of the Phanerozoic Eon.

Five major historical global extinction events (Ordovician-Silurian, Late Devonian, Permian-Triassic, Triassic-Jurassic, Cretaceous-Paleogene). The Permian-Triassic ('Great Dying') wiped out ~96% of marine species.
A massive igneous province located on the Deccan Plateau of west-central India, formed by extensive flood basalt eruptions at the end of the Cretaceous period (~66 million years ago).
The official body responsible for defining Earth's geological time scale, setting global standard stratotypes (GSSPs - 'Golden Spikes').

items.title: Major Geological Divisions of India
items.content:
• **Peninsular Block**: Stable Precambrian shield comprising ancient cratons (Aravalli, Dharwar, Singhbhum, Bastar, Bundelkhand), largely immune to major folding.
• **Extra-Peninsular / Himalayan Belt**: Dynamic, unstable young fold mountains formed during the Cenozoic Era via collision of Indian and Eurasian plates.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Complex stratigraphic correlations in complex terrains; ongoing scientific debates regarding the formalization of the **Anthropocene** epoch.
• **Policy Interventions**: Geological Survey of India (GSI) mapping missions, National Geoscience Data Repository (NGDR) for resource exploration and hazard mitigation.

items.title: Mnemonic for Phanerozoic Eras (Old to Young)
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **P**lease **M**ake **C**offee
• **Decoded Meaning**: **P**aleozoic -> **M**esozoic -> **C**enozoic
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly recalls the correct chronological sequence of the three most recent major biological eras.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember 'HAPPC' for Eons in order: **H**adean, **A**rchean, **P**roterozoic (Precambrian) followed by **P**hanerozoic and the current **C**enozoic emphasis.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently tests whether dinosaurs existed in the Paleozoic era. Remember, dinosaurs evolved in the Mesozoic era (Triassic period) and went extinct at the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary, long before humans appeared in the Cenozoic era.

Mains Value Addition: In answers related to Indian Agriculture or Mineral Resources, link them directly to geological history (e.g., 'Peninsular India's mineral wealth is a direct consequence of Archean cratonization and Dharwar system metamorphism').

keyTakeaways: Earth's history is divided into hierarchical units (Eons, Eras, Periods, Epochs) calibrated via stratigraphy and fossil records.
India's geology neatly reflects its journey from the ancient Gondwanaland craton to its northward drift and collision with Eurasia.
Understanding geological eras is essential for solving questions on mineral distribution, fossil fuels, and physiographic evolution in UPSC exams.
